prompt: Desktop web application screen for Eco-Nomz, the Indonesian marketplace that helps restaurants sell surplus food, rendered edge to edge at 1440 by 900 with sharp readable text and no browser frame. The visitor is a restaurant owner setting up a required square logo from a landscape 1200 by 750 PNG; square uploads should skip cropping. Keep the existing Eco-Nomz logo and name, familiar navigation, green and orange brand colors, and English/Indonesian utility. Show a slim four-step progress sequence near the top, then let the crop interaction lead: a generous, nearly full-width editing canvas with a square crop boundary, visible corner handles, darkened image outside the square, and comfortable controls for rotate left, rotate right, reset, and zoom. Place a quieter but prominent right-side panel with a square logo preview that clearly reflects the selected crop, the PNG/JPEG and 10 MB limit, and a plain note that the logo is required before publishing. Keep the title direct—Position your logo—and explain that dragging chooses what customers see. Put Select a different file and Apply crop and continue at the bottom of the work area. The screen should feel focused, reassuring, and operational, not like a marketing hero or an upload dashboard. Maintain a clear reading order from progress, to crop, to preview, to the next action.
